title: What Happens When You Stand Up Too Fast?
description:
Send this to the friend who sees stars every time they get off the couch.
When you stand up suddenly, gravity pulls about half a liter to a liter of blood into the veins of your legs and trunk (Merck Manual). Your blood pressure dips for a moment, which can make you dizzy or blur your vision, until sensors near your heart and neck arteries tell your heart to beat faster (Mayo Clinic). People call it a head rush, but the blood is actually heading down. Get up slowly, and if it happens often, or you faint or fall, talk to a doctor (NHS, Cleveland Clinic).
